It was the first time I made a fork, opened a pull request, and merged code on a repo that wasn’t mine.

articles.title: Leaked images reveal Motorola’s wide foldable
articles.summary:
New leaked images of Motorola’s next folding smartphone shared by SammyGuru add more credence to the theory that widescreen could be the default design for foldables moving forward. Following a single leaked shot shared to Reddit yesterday, this new crop of images reveal the Motorola Razr Flex from several angles in two finishes with its inner screen completely open and partially folded.
Leaked images reveal Motorola’s wide foldable
The Razr Flex will compete with the iPhone Duo, Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, and other widescreen folding devices.
The photos show the Razr Flex in two finishes: coriander brown and dark botanical garden, according to SammyGuru. The brown option features a back panel with a bumpy leather-like finish, while the green has a fabric-like woven finish. The cover screen has a hole-punch selfie camera centered at the top, while the Razr Flex’s inner screen pushes the camera to the upper right corner. On the back is a pill-shaped bar with two cameras and a flash.
The Flex is expected to be a smaller and more affordable alternative to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, which has a 5.5-inch cover screen and a 7.6-inch main display when unfolded. But more specific details — including the size of the Razr Flex, its pricing, and when it’s expected to be debut — are still unknown.

articles.title: AI isn’t replacing your job. It’s turning it into low-paid gig work
articles.summary:
The gig economy has arrived for cardiologists. Recruiting platform Outlier, run by Scale AI, advertises offers of up to $180 an hour for physicians in the U.S. to design complex cardiac scenarios, review artificial intelligence-generated reports, and rank model outputs. The site offers up to $7.50 an hour for Tagalog work in the Philippines for the same job, and up to $12.50 an hour for Swahili in Tanzania.
Companies like Scale AI first outsourced data work to wherever labor was cheapest. Now, they are recruiting physicians, lawyers, and Ph.D.s to generate and annotate data, rank model answers, and verify outputs. Higher credentials can raise the advertised rate, but the platform still controls payment and working conditions.
I’ve spent the last six years interviewing the people who do this work. Most were in Venezuela, where economic collapse has left a large, educated population online and out of options. One of them, Rogelio, taught computer science until the economic crisis and the pandemic left his family without work. His 13-year-old son discovered they could earn money labeling images of cars and roads on the platforms Hive and Scale AI’s Remotasks, using a laptop the Hugo Chávez government had issued to schoolchildren a decade earlier. The boy made 18 cents for a few hours of work. Rogelio joined him and made just over $2 on his first day.
For a while, the work paid. A task called Beast Mode where workers labeled objects in people’s homes paid more than any other work…

articles.title: Java4Shell Exploitation Attempts Begin as Vendors Rush Out Advisories
articles.summary:
Threat actors have started targeting the recently disclosed Java4Shell vulnerability, as more vendors publish advisories detailing the flaw’s impact on their products.
Tracked as CVE-2026-114938, Java4Shell is a memory corruption bug in the way OpenJDK 17.0.6 and newer handle Base64 data. Exploitation requires an x86-64 processor supporting AVX-512 VBMI, a feature found in newer Intel and AMD CPUs. ARM-based systems are not affected.
Calif disclosed the bug on November 17, the same day Oracle and the OpenJDK project released patches.
Calif said it achieved unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) against the default configurations of Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Keycloak and other enterprise applications. However, it noted that no single exploit works against all of them, and that each needs a tailored attack chain.
Attackers are probing for vulnerable systems
As of early November 19, threat intelligence firm GreyNoise had recorded over 150 requests matching the shape of a Java4Shell attack, coming from five IP addresses. The company has not seen any successful intrusions on its sensors.
WatchTowr has also seen activity. “We are already seeing attackers spray the internet and hit our global honeypot network with requests decorated in ‘java4shell-recon’ User-Agents, alongside blind exploitation attempts using correctly shaped requests,” said Jake Knott, head of threat intelligence at WatchTowr.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
- November 4, 2026
- Source:
- Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. Just as a quick note, the official Top500 post says there were 27 new systems, but when we filtered the list on First Appearance 68 (with 68 being the November 2026 list), we got 28 new systems. The previous low was 39 in June 2022, and while November 2024 rebounded to 54, this edition represents a clear step down.
The June 2018 list had 133 new systems, and November 2018 had 153. Those days of roughly a quarter or more of the list turning over with each publication are long gone. Today’s 28 newcomers represent 5.6% of the full Top500.
The 28 new systems together contribute about 1.0 EF/s of Rmax, or roughly 5.1% of the list’s total performance. That is the lowest share since at least November 2021, when new systems contributed over 12%. The prior low was 5.48% in June 2023, so this continues a pattern in which even the systems that do get submitted add little aggregate HPL capability. articles.title: Al menos el 10% de la población mundial sufre un uso problemático de internet: “Hay que priorizar la salud pública frente a la industria”
articles.summary:
Al menos el 10% de la población mundial sufre un uso problemático de internet: “Hay que priorizar la salud pública frente a la industria”
La revista ‘The Lancet’ urge a gobiernos a actuar para combatir los trastornos por apuestas y videojuegos en línea, el consumo adictivo del porno o la hipocondría que genera la red
Existe un término. Se inventó durante la década de los noventa y se llama “adicción a internet”. Pero ya no es suficiente, se ha quedado obsoleto. Por ello, la Comisión de la prestigiosa revista The Lancet Psychiatry ha decidido emplear otro: “Uso problemático de internet” (PUI, en inglés). Y las razones no son muy halagüeñas. En un documento publicado este jueves, la Comisión estima que el PUI afecta al menos al 10% de la población mundial. Una situación que abarca desde los trastornos por apuestas y videojuegos en línea, pasando por el consumo adictivo del porno, hasta llegar a conductas “emergentes” como la cibercondría —los hipocondriacos de siempre, solo que ahora potenciados por las infinitas y aterradoras posibilidades de la red—. Los autores del artículo urgen a los gobiernos y a todas las instituciones involucradas a “priorizar la salud pública por encima de los intereses de la industria”.

articles.title: Internet traffic and attacks during the 2026 U.S. midterm elections
articles.summary:
Internet traffic and attacks during the 2026 U.S. midterm elections
Visitors to government election websites surged 363% on November 3, the date of the 2026 midterm elections in the United States. Across Cloudflare's election protection programs, we also detected a significant shift in the types and timing of cyberattacks throughout 2026.
Unlike what we saw in other recent elections, attackers focused on gaining access to internal systems and data, rather than knocking websites offline. Government election websites faced website vulnerability attempts 180 times more often than denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks, and at roughly ten times the rate of Cloudflare's broader customer base. We also found evidence of at least one attempt to exploit a recently disclosed critical PHP vulnerability on a state government voting website in the Western United States.
These attacks peaked in late October, several weeks before the election. Vulnerability exploit attempts climbed steadily throughout 2026: from 200,000 per day in January, to 2 million per day in October. However, on Election Day in the U.S., Cloudflare detected no escalation in attack volume and zero major DDoS incidents across protected election sites, marking a sharp contrast to other recent elections, such as in Moldova last year.
Our data regarding cyberattacks on election institutions came from organizations participating in Cloudflare's free cybersecurity programs: the Athenian Project, Cloudflare for Campaigns, and Projec…

articles.title: F5 Patches Critical NGINX2Root Flaws as PoC Exploits Go Public
articles.summary:
F5 on Wednesday announced patches for 22 vulnerabilities, including five critical-severity NGINX bugs that could lead to unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE).
Referred to as NGINX2Root, the five issues are tracked as CVE-2026-113425, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633, and CVE-2026-123634 (CVSS score of 9.2).
CVE-2026-113425 affects NGINX instances configured as mail proxy servers and can be exploited via specially crafted mail sessions. CVE-2026-121810 can be exploited on servers that use HTTP/3 to trigger a use-after-free in the NGINX worker process.
CVE-2026-123634 impacts servers configured as proxies and can be triggered if the proxied server name includes variables, and a subrequest to a location resolving that server name is received from a Server Side Includes (SSI) or mirror directive.
CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 require HTTP/2 to be enabled on an affected server. Successful exploitation of the former leads to a buffer overflow, while the latter triggers a use-after-free in the worker process.
The two issues were independently reported by Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, Wiz, and Xint. They explain that attackers could exploit them to run commands with the privileges of the nginx worker process and fully compromise the server.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
- November 7, 2026
- Source:
- University of Regensburg
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.

A tool call can arrive in pieces, an argument can be cut short, or model-specific markup can leak into the answer. A frontend parser turns that output, received as token IDs or decoded text, into visible text, reasoning, and tool calls an application can use.
In this post, you’ll learn how tool-call parsing works and use an AI agent to build a parser for a new model. You’ll start with a weather request and a human-reviewed test set, using frontend-crates, the reusable Rust components behind NVIDIA Dynamo tool-calling parsers.
Suppose you ask for the weather in Paris. The model may generate reasoning followed by a get_weather call with a city argument. The frontend prepares and tokenizes the prompt, then an inference engine runs the LLM to generate tokens. The parser consumes token IDs or decoded text and separates reasoning, visible text, and tool calls in order. A protocol adapter turns those events into an OpenAI-compatible response, using the same parsing path for batch JSON and streaming updates.
The tricky part is recognizing where each piece starts and ends. A call can be malformed or incomplete, a marker can appear inside an argument, or ordinary text can surround the call. The parser has to handle these boundaries without losing data, duplicating calls, or leaking model-specific markup.

OpenAI has sparked a backlash in the mathematics community by apparently using AI to solve more than 700 longstanding maths problems in a short space of time. A recent open letter signed by 28 recipients of the Fields Medal (one of the highest honours in maths) goes some way to explaining why.
Mathematicians who have gone through some of the solutions offered by AI say they are opaque in their reasoning. As the open letter explains: “Solving problems is only a tool and proxy for achieving the primary goal of conceptual understanding and insight.”
As famed mathematician and Fields Medal winner Terence Tao put it: “These companies are dumping carcasses of raw meat onto our communal village table and saying: ‘Here you go, I solved your food problem.‘”
OpenAI said it had consulted with the community prior to announcing the latest three results, one of which was in my own field of computer science.
Nevertheless, mathematicians are having to adapt fast to the disruptive arrival of AI in their field. This challenge extends far beyond mathematics and into all other disciplines of science and research.
The impact AI has had on software development through tools such as Claude and Codex, is undeniable. Industry software teams are now routinely using AI tools in their work.
But now, AI is already having a major impact on the practice of science itself. Academic journals and conferences are dealing with exponential increases in submissions from researchers, in a system largely based on v…

Physicist Yiwen Chu and her team have developed a system that uses microscopic mechanical vibrations to store and manipulate quantum information, much like the vibrating strings of a guitar produce musical notes.
Unlike the sounds produced by a musical instrument, these vibrations occur at frequencies far beyond human hearing. They take place within a tiny quantum chip, where they serve as a new form of computer memory.
By harnessing these vibrations, the researchers have created a way for quantum computers to process information efficiently while accessing a flexible working memory. "The interaction between the quantum processor and the quantum memory provides a crucial foundation with a view to establishing quantum computers as a powerful and reliable way to perform computations that are not feasible with conventional computers," says Yiwen Chu.

articles.title: PesaLink’s bank owners remain split on what it should cost

Gituku Kirika runs a payments network owned by Kenya’s banks, but he cannot dictate what they charge customers.
This constraint defines PesaLink’s efforts to win everyday payments from mobile money services. Launched in 2017, PesaLink allows customers to send up to KES 999,999 ($7,700) instantly between bank accounts at different financial institutions. The network is operated by Integrated Payment Services Limited (IPSL), which Kirika leads. The Kenya Bankers Association (KBA), the industry body representing the country’s lenders, is its sole shareholder.
PesaLink says it processes an average of KES 4 billion ($30.8 million) daily, up 24% from 2025. Monthly transaction value has reached KES 110 billion ($846.5 million), up 41% year on year. The company reports a transaction success rate of about 98%.
This year, IPSL has been encouraging banks to adopt a common transfer fee: free for transactions of KES 1,000 ($7.70) or less, and a flat KES 20 ($0.15) for larger transfers, up to KES 999,999 ($7,700). Sending KES 50,000 ($384) between bank accounts costs just KES 20, compared with KES 108 ($0.83) through M-PESA or Airtel Money.
KCB, Co-operative Bank, NCBA, Absa and Stanbic have adopted the flat-fee model. Equity Bank, Standard Chartered and I&M have not, leaving their customers on tiered pricing, where transfer fees rise with the amount sent.
Kirika says PesaLink can only recommend a price, not impose one, but he expects all banks to switch before the end of 2027.

Multiple designs are emerging for CPO and NPO, but standardization and high-volume manufacturing are still not ready.

As photonics shifts from pluggable optical transceivers toward near- and co-packaged optics (NPO, CPO), engineers are devising new ways to attach fibers to the photonics chips on a board. Several different designs exist today, but so far there is no common interface.
With pluggable photonics, lasers and connections are attached at the server faceplate, with the board itself housing only electronic components. Yet long electrical connections to the faceplate mean higher power and longer latency. Fibers would need to move onto the interior of the board to solve that. That eliminates the need for pluggables, but it requires new solutions.
“With the rapid growth of generative AI, AI data centers are required to process enormous volumes of data faster and more efficiently than ever before,” said Yoshimasa Bando, principal scientist at Mitsubishi Chemical. “To meet this demand, further improvements in communication speed and energy efficiency have become critical challenges.”
The goal of CPO and NPO is to reduce reliance on long electrical connections.
Long lines
One reason for maintaining faceplate pluggables is that lasers are not always reliable. Using a pluggable module makes it easy to replace the laser.

articles.title: The Governance Gap in Open-Weight AI and What to Do About It
articles.summary:
Open-weight AI has gone mainstream. As of September 2026, some estimates suggest 42% of enterprises surveyed were running open-weight models in production, up from 31% just two months earlier. But downloading a model also means taking on responsibilities that a provider might otherwise handle, and many organizations have yet to put clear ownership and controls in place.
Renting Capability Vs. Running Your Own Copy
When you use an AI model through a provider’s app or service, you’re essentially renting its capabilities. The provider controls the model and handles the infrastructure, updates, and safety controls. You access it through an app or a software connection.
An open-weight AI model makes its learned parameters, the ‘weights’ that shape its behavior, available to download and run yourself. You can run the model on your own infrastructure and adapt it for a particular use case using your own data. The license may limit how you can use it, and running it still carries infrastructure and staffing costs.
Open-weight models are becoming more capable. One estimate puts the best open-weight models roughly four months behind leading models.
Open-weight does not necessarily mean open-source. Access to the weights does not guarantee access to the training code or details of the training data.
When Benefits Clash with Risks

The new Edge Lockdown Mode offers optional, extreme protections for users facing highly targeted attacks who are willing to sacrifice website compatibility for stronger defenses.
"Lockdown Mode is designed for users who are at particular risk of being targeted in cybersecurity campaigns. This may include journalists, executives, security researchers, and administrators," said Partner Security Group Manager Gareth Evans.
"Individuals whose threat model justifies accepting reduced compatibility in exchange for stronger protection. It may also apply to devices operating within highly restricted environments."
Evans also warned that websites that use the disabled APIs (especially those with interactive graphics like games or maps) may not work as expected when this security feature is toggled on.

articles.title: Enabling Real-Time AI for Scientific Instruments with GPU-Native Data Acquisition | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
In science and industry, analyzing sensor measurements in real time can enable AI to adjust processes, guide experiments, and search for better operating conditions. Yet limits on how quickly the measured data can be moved and processed often shape how an instrument is designed, from readout electronics to acquisition timing. What could scientific instrument makers simplify—or make possible—if processing could keep pace with their sensors?

It enables developers to process measurements during acquisition without first writing them to disk. Most Kenyan businesses that buy from China pay through their banks, which usually convert the money into dollars on the way. That pushes up transaction costs, a burden for importers working on thin margins. WapiPay is offering a direct shilling-to-yuan route that skips the dollar.
“Our work with WeChat Pay helped lay the groundwork,” Paul Ndichu, WapiPay co-founder, said in a statement. “With Alipay, we’re opening another payment route and positioning WapiPay to serve a market with an estimated $300 billion in annual flows.”
Kenyan importers are heavy buyers of Chinese currency and have little yuan income to offset it, meaning every payment has to be funded by selling shillings, directly or through the dollar. The high number of new and upcoming production lines is a unique factor influencing this particular cycle.
Global silicon wafer shipments are forecast to grow 11.8% in 2026, according to the Q3 2026 SEMI Silicon Wafer Market Monitor. This increase is primarily due to strong demand for AI, which is projected to drive shipments through 2029.
Alongside AI, rising process material sales are also supporting recovery. The positive correlation between material sales and silicon wafer demand not only reflects growth in manufacturing complexity, but it also points to greater material consumption per wafer.
Finally, increases in memory demand, precautionary inventory building, and global fab capacity expansions are boosting silicon wafer shipments as well.
To better understand today’s landscape, it’s helpful to revisit past silicon wafer demand curves. From 2018 to 2019 and from 2022 to 2023, silicon wafer shipments rose ahead of major increases in memory work-in-process (WIP) inventories, or unfinished memory chips undergoing fabrication. However, shipments lagged at the same time WIP inventory peaked. Because fabrication lines were already producing at full capacity, their need for silicon wafers slowed.
While this pattern provides historical context for today’s demand recovery, the high number of new and upcoming production lines is a unique factor influencing this particular cycle.

In the months leading up to the vote, trade groups and human rights advocates have raised concerns about the risks of blocking cellphone signals in prisons. articles.title: Reducing Rollout Bottlenecks in Reinforcement Learning with NVIDIA Dynamo | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Reinforcement learning (RL) uses rewards to train models to solve problems and complete tasks more successfully.
Inference drives this process. Workers generate rollouts: sequences of model outputs, actions, and environment interactions. The RL framework scores the results, updates model weights, and sends those weights back to the workers for the next round.
As RL training scales, redundant compute work, slow rollouts, weight updates, and worker failures can waste GPU capacity and delay training.
NVIDIA Dynamo provides the serving layer to address these constraints, helping teams generate more accepted training samples and complete training iterations faster.
This blog post explains the rollout bottlenecks that slow RL training and how Dynamo addresses them through routing, ModelExpress weight updates, and recovery.
1. Why RL needs distributed rollout infrastructure
A reasoning rollout may contain one response. A coding-agent rollout can involve repository exploration, edits, tool calls, and tests. These differences create an uneven workload across inference workers.
Three constraints determine how effectively that workload supports training.
Rollout completion time. When training requires a group of samples, the slowest required rollout can delay the next step. Distributing request counts evenly across GPUs does not necessarily distribute work evenly.

Two critical NGINX vulnerabilities dubbed "nginx2root" allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely on vulnerable web servers, with researchers demonstrating how the flaws can be chained with a Linux kernel bug to gain root access.
The two HTTP/2 vulnerabilities were discovered independently by researchers at Xint, Wiz, Ikotas Labs, Metnir, and Rapid7, while Xint also discovered three additional NGINX RCE flaws.
Censys later reproduced the underlying memory corruption conditions in four of the five flaws through lab testing, but did not achieve remote code execution.
The first of the two "nginx2root" flaws is CVE-2026-123007, a flow-control bug that can corrupt memory in an NGINX worker. It impacts all versions from 1.31.8 down to 1.9.5, released in 2015.
Wiz demonstrated unauthenticated remote code execution on a server hosting ordinary static files over HTTP/2 with TLS, while Xint demoed root access by chaining it with a separate Linux kernel flaw.
Xint says the separate vulnerability affects the Linux kernel's SCTP subsystem and can be used to escape an NGINX Docker container and gain root privileges on the underlying host.
The second flaw is CVE-2026-123633, a use-after-free problem that affects NGINX when it accepts HTTP/2 connections and proxies requests to a backend. It impacts all versions from 1.19.7 through 1.31.8.

articles.title: Google is putting AI chats right on the homepage
articles.summary:
Google is updating its homepage to include AI searches. In a post on X, Google’s vice president of product, Robby Stein, shows how you can now open a collapsible sidebar to view and continue your AI chats.
Google is putting AI chats right on the homepage
You can now view your recent AI searches by opening the sidebar on Google’s homepage.
Based on the GIF shared by Stein, it looks like you can open the sidebar by clicking the gray bar that appears on the left side of your screen. From there, Google will show a list of the searches you’ve made using AI Mode, along with the ability to start a new thread, search your threads, or connect a Gemini Notebook.
It’s yet another big change for Google’s homepage, which has long presented you with a single bar to kick off your web search. The company brought its AI Mode button to its search bar last year, which opens up a chatbot-like search experience within Google. In May, Google updated its search box to accommodate longer queries and added AI-powered autocomplete.
Stein says Google is rolling out the option because “people are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done,” adding that “in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web.” The new homepage is rolling out globally on desktop.

articles.title: iFood sofre ataque hacker, que expõe dados de clientes e entregadores

O iFood confirmou que sofreu ataque hacker que expôs dados cadastrais de clientes, entregadores e representantes de restaurantes parceiros. A invasão aconteceu em 14 de novembro e a empresa começou a comunicar as pessoas afetadas por e-mail nesta quinta-feira (19).
A companhia ainda investiga o incidente e não informou quantas pessoas tiveram informações acessadas pelos criminosos. Apesar da invasão, os serviços da plataforma continuam funcionando normalmente.
Em comunicado, o iFood afirmou que os invasores não conseguiram acessar senhas, cartões de crédito, outros meios de pagamento, saldos, extratos bancários ou informações biométricas.
A empresa também informou que, até o momento, não identificou evidências de divulgação ou uso indevido dos dados acessados. A apuração continua em andamento.
“O iFood notificou a Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD) e colabora com a autoridade. A investigação e o monitoramento continuam”, declarou a companhia.
Quais dados foram expostos no ataque ao iFood?
As informações acessadas pelos criminosos variam conforme o tipo de cadastro. Clientes, entregadores e representantes de restaurantes tiveram diferentes dados pessoais expostos.
Confira o que pode ter sido comprometido:
- Clientes e usuários do iFood Benefícios: apenas números de telefone, sem exposição de nomes, CPFs, e-mails ou endereços;

articles.summary:
Something to look forward to: Microsoft is testing an experimental open-source AMD shader compiler in the Xbox Game Development Kit, marking a major change in the way game consoles are optimized. Redmond believes that the update will improve game performance by 2% to 16% on current-gen Xbox consoles.
The open-source AMD compiler at the heart of the updated GDK is based on ACO, a shader compiler from the Mesa project that is used by the RADV Vulkan driver for AMD GPUs on Linux. It converts high-level shader instructions into machine code optimized for RDNA 2 GPUs powering Xbox Series X|S, Steam Deck, and other gaming handhelds.
Developed by the open-source Linux community in collaboration with Valve and independent developers, the compiler will replace the older LLVM-based architecture, enabling much faster shader compilation and yielding smoother runtime performance in Vulkan games on the Steam Deck and Linux PCs.

Java, the programming language that Oracle has always claimed is on billions of devices, has a critical security vulnerability that allows for remote code execution (RCE), often without even needing to log in to the application. The consequence is that an attacker can gain access to the target system, read user and internal data, and have a launch point for further shenanigans, including database access and potential system takeover.

Last year, Bob was sitting in his hospital bed talking with his family and joking with his nurse as he recovered from surgery. But by midnight, Bob was back on a breathing machine and rushed into surgery. By morning, he was dead.
“The worst feeling as an intensivist is when the alarms only ring when it’s too late and you lose a patient.”
Dr. Bijan Teja,
AI Compass
“The worst feeling as an intensivist is when the alarms only ring when it’s too late and you lose a patient,” Teja, an ICU doctor at St. Michael’s Hospital in Toronto, said.
Teja has been working with Dr. Michael Sklar, his best friend at the hospital, on a new tool that might have been able to save Bob’s life: AI Compass. It will be fed data on tens of thousands of ICU patients to identify imperceptible patterns that emerge in patients’ health before they take a turn for the worse, potentially giving doctors more time to save a life.
“Bijan and I, as ICU doctors, think we know the patterns that exist when someone may deteriorate, and alternatively, when someone may be improving,” Sklar said. “Is it possible that there are signs in the data that we’re collecting that we just don’t know yet … that could signify deterioration?”

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Cisco Expressway Vulnerability Soon After PoC Release

Hackers exploited a critical Cisco Expressway vulnerability to breach a Russian organization soon after proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit code was released publicly, according to cybersecurity firm F6.
Expressway gateways allow remote employees, partners, and third-party users to securely connect to an organization’s collaboration services, including video calls, voice calls, and instant messaging.
Tracked as CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS score of 9.8), the flaw can be exploited without authentication by remote attackers with network access to a device, allowing them to execute commands as root. It affects virtual and appliance versions of Expressway Core and Expressway Edge, but only when the devices are clustered.
Cisco, which disclosed the issue on October 21, said it resides in the Expressway database service feature and stems from persistent cookies.
An attacker possessing the persistent cookies could reach the database service and issue certain remote procedure call (RPC) commands, gaining the ability to run root-level commands on the underlying operating system.
Expressway X15.5.20 resolves the vulnerability. There are no workarounds, and customers on X14 or earlier releases need to move to a fixed release, Cisco says.
The advisory has not been revised since its initial release and still states that Cisco is unaware of public announcements or malicious use of the flaw. However, a PoC exploit has since been posted on GitHub, and F6 says the attack it investigated came shortly after…

articles.title: Robots can do backflips but can't hold a gaze or press piano keys, and scientists think they've fixed that
articles.summary:
What just happened? Engineers at the University of Pennsylvania have built an artificial muscle fiber that tracks its own temperature and corrects itself, so it can hold a precise position instead of slowly drifting back to its resting shape. The fiber pairs a rubber-like liquid crystal elastomer with graphene and an ultrathin copper coil that works as both a heater and a sensor. In lab tests, the muscles let a robot hand strike piano keys with different amounts of force and let a pair of robotic eyes hold a steady gaze.
The work, published in Advanced Functional Materials, is modeled on the small muscles that move human fingers and eyes. Those muscles make fine, controlled movements, and that kind of control has been hard to get from the hardware inside most robots today.
Large humanoid robots usually run on bulky, rigid motors and mechanical parts. That setup is good enough for walking and lifting, but not for small, careful motions. It's a familiar problem in robotics. Machines that can dance or do acrobatic flips still struggle with jobs people find easy, like folding laundry or keeping their eyes fixed on one spot.
Moving to soft materials brings its own trade-off. "Soft robotic muscles need to be both strong and flexible to mimic human movements, but these properties are rarely found in the same material," said Shu Yang, a University of Pennsylvania engineer and co-author of the study, in a statement.

In the first quarter of 2026, it estimated that 23.1% of South Africans aged 15 to 64 had used a generative artificial intelligence (AI) tool, followed by 10.1% of Nigerians and 8.7% of Kenyans. One shows how popular ChatGPT is among people who already use the internet. The other estimates how far a range of generative AI tools has reached across the working-age population. articles.summary:
Ask many IT teams how they would recognize ransomware, and the answer is still “when files start changing extensions.” By then, the intrusion may already include credential theft, privilege escalation, defense evasion, recovery sabotage, lateral movement and data exfiltration.
Encryption is often a late-stage action, not the beginning of the attack. In data-extortion attacks it never happens at all: the operators steal data and threaten to leak it without encrypting anything.
Recent attacks against on-premises SharePoint servers illustrate that sequence. After exploiting internet-facing systems, operators used stolen credentials and legitimate administration tools to move through victim environments before deploying ransomware.
The practical lesson is simple: defenders need to detect the behaviors that precede encryption, not only the encryptor itself.

Mehr als ein Jahrzehnt unerkannt: Gravierende Sicherheitslücke in Nginx entdeckt
Eine Reihe von Cybersecurity-Unternehmen hat eine Sicherheitslücke in Nginx entdeckt. Dabei handelt es sich um die Webserver-Software, die von zahlreichen Webseiten genutzt wird. Laut „Built with it“ sind es mittlerweile mehr als 65 Millionen Seiten, darunter die Webauftritte von Mastercard, Morgan Stanley und Logitech.
Wie gravierend ist die Nginx-Sicherheitslücke?
Zu den Sicherheitsforscher:innen, die den Fehler gefunden haben, zählen unter anderem die Expert:innen von Wiz Research, Ikotas Labs und Metnir. Wie Wiz schreibt, handelt es sich im Grunde um zwei kritische Sicherheitslücken, die aber dieselben Auswirkungen haben. Werden sie ausgenutzt, können Server kompromittiert werden. Angreifer:innen haben dann die Möglichkeit, Schadcode aus der Ferne auszuführen, Daten zu stehlen, die betriebenen Webseiten zu verändern oder deren Betrieb zu stören.
Eine der Sicherheitslücken mit der Kennung CVE-2026-123633 soll sich schon mehr als sechs Jahre unbemerkt in Nginx verbergen, die andere sogar zehn Jahre (CVE-2026-123007). Wiz schreibt dazu: „Beide Fehler sind Speichersicherheitsfehler bei Nginx Handhabung von HTTP/2-Traffic. Bei CVE-2026-123633 wird der für eine Verbindung benötigte Speicher schon freigegeben, obwohl er noch genutzt wird, wodurch ein Use-after-Free entsteht. Bei CVE-2026-123007 sorgt eine falsche Flow-Kontrolle für eine ungültige Speicherkopierung.“

articles.title: A human liver has been kept alive outside the body for a record seven weeks
articles.summary:
A human liver has been kept alive outside the body for a record seven weeks
Technology called “machine perfusion” is creating the chance for more transplants—and daring new science.
Researchers in Australia claim they’ve kept a human liver alive, on life support, outside the body for seven weeks, opening up speculative new possibilities in biomedical engineering.
The feat, whose details are pending publication, was carried out in Sydney after a team led by surgeon and inventor Carlo Pulitano connected a donated liver to a system of automated pumps and sensors that fed the organ nutrients, supplied it with blood, and whisked away waste.
In an interview, Pulitano, a transplant surgeon at the Royal Prince Alfred Hospital and a professor at the University of Sydney, likened the life support system to “an artificial body.” Its official name is the Extended Organ Perfusion System.
“Our group is the only one in the world to have maintained a human liver under fully normothermic, physiological conditions for seven weeks,” he says.
Normothermic means body temperature, or about 37 °C. The previous record for keeping an internal organ alive outside the body was set in Switzerland several years ago. That organ—also a liver—lasted around two weeks.
Most organs destined for transplant survive only a few hours in special ice buckets and need to be raced to their destination. Over the last decade, however, surgeons have been switching to perfusion systems, which pump warm or cold fluids into…

articles.title: What employee adoption of Shadow AI is telling the enterprise
articles.summary:
What employee adoption of Shadow AI is telling the enterprise
Many employees are already choosing their own AI tools
Across industries, businesses are putting approved AI tools into the hands of employees, but many employees are already choosing their own.
Microsoft research found that 71% of UK employees have used unapproved consumer AI tools at work, and more than half use them every week.
For 41%, these are tools they already use in their personal lives, while more than a quarter say their employer offers no approved alternative.
Chief Evangelist at Kore.ai
This is the Shadow AI economy. It creates an obvious security challenge, but it also shows where demand already exists.
Employees are choosing these tools because they are finding practical value in them, often before their employers have caught up.
Why Shadow AI persists
Providing an approved AI tool doesn't automatically change the habits employees have already formed. Consumer AI has set expectations around speed, flexibility and ease of experimentation. Employees can try different approaches, move between tasks and use the technology for whatever they need to get done.
Approved enterprise AI has to meet a different set of requirements. It needs to protect company data, respect access controls, integrate with existing systems and operate within governance requirements. But employees still expect it to be just as useful and easy to use.

articles.title: AI Accelerators Drive Changes In Power Delivery Networks
articles.summary:
Moving voltage regulators closer to processors can reduce power loss, but adds challenges for advanced packaging, thermal management, and system-level design.
Key Takeaways:
Power delivery is now a significant performance limiter in data center chips. The demands of AI and high-performance computing chips running near 0.7 V for a 600W GPU are forcing current to rise to 1,000 amps and beyond, compounding resistive losses and voltage droop across the PDN. Multi-chiplet constructions only compound these issues by further increasing current density and signal congestion.
To solve these challenges, designers are turning to vertical power delivery networks, where the voltage regulator modules are relocated much closer to the processors from their position on the device periphery — to the PCB landside (under the PCB), inside the accelerator package, or inside the silicon interposer. Together with the growing customization of AI accelerator modules, there are many approaches on offer with varying design and manufacturing complexity.
The vertical PDN trend began nearly a decade ago with the integration of backside power delivery networks (BPDNs) on the wafer backside, enabling fine-tuned power delivery more directly to the transistors while reducing IR drop across the tens of interconnect levels on-chip. articles.title: NetWasm 0.10 Speeds Up C# on WebAssembly, Now Faster Than Mono AOT
articles.summary:
The team behind NetWasm has published a write-up of its 0.10 optimisation work, spanning releases 0.10.1 to 0.10.8. The changes touch exception handling, array bounds checks, WebAssembly SIMD and integer division. On the project’s own benchmark set, NetWasm now comes out ahead of Mono AOT and gets close to desktop .NET on some workloads.
NetWasm is a compiler and runtime that compiles C# programs ahead of time into small, standalone WebAssembly files. It takes the IL that Roslyn produces and emits Wasm, using its own runtime and a CoreLib ported from .NET. The yardstick is the Mono AOT build for WASI, which runs .NET on the same engine. A new garbage collector had already put NetWasm in front on allocation-heavy code, but plain loops were still slower: a quicksort of 100,000 integers took 77.2 ms, against 58.0 ms for Mono AOT.
Much of the early gain came from exception handling in 0.10.1. Wasmtime adds extra register save-and-restore code around any function that can throw or catch, floating-point registers included. Methods with null, bounds or checked-arithmetic checks paid that price on every call. Throws now go through a shared function and the catching handler releases the frames, which cut UI churn from 17.6 to 7.9 ms.

articles.title: Nvidia's latest drivers may be wearing out your SSD with tens of gigabytes of unnecessary writes
articles.summary:
TL;DR: Users who have recently updated their Nvidia display drivers should check the Resource Monitor's Disk tab to see whether an executable called NVDisplay.Container.exe is writing excessively to the disk. Nvidia had not acknowledged the issue at the time of writing, but reports claim that it now writes tens of gigabytes per day, which might shorten an SSD's lifespan. Until Nvidia provides a fix, rolling back to driver version 621.01 is the only foolproof remedy.
TroubleGrid recently published a summary of the issue, which impacts driver versions 621.14 and 621.24, both released in November. Besides rolling back drivers, users can restart the affected service or change the display container settings, but neither solution is perfect.
The problem occurs because the display container service now rewrites its log instead of appending to it, exponentially increasing the amount of data written to the SSD. Users can confirm whether they are experiencing the issue by opening the Resource Monitor app, clicking the Disk tab, and searching for a process called "NVDisplay.Container.exe" to see how much data it is writing in bytes.
While some users report the figure holding steady at around 20 MB, others report it writing dozens of gigabytes each day, even while idle. SSDs start breaking down after writing a certain amount of data, usually measured in hundreds of terabytes, so it's best to monitor how much each program writes.

Transport for London (TfL) has announced that around 265,000 Oyster photocard customers may have had their account details exposed in a data breach.
TfL is London's public transport authority, operating the Underground, Overground, buses, trams, and the Elizabeth line. It recorded 3.53 billion passenger journeys in 2025/26, including 1.78 billion bus journeys and 1.20 billion Tube journeys.
Oyster photocards are travel smartcards with the holder's photo that give eligible passengers free or discounted travel.
The organization discovered the security incident on November 16, 2026, after receiving customer reports about emails requesting them to create an account, which came directly from TfL's mail systems as a result of a compromise.
The Oyster photocard website has now been taken offline and the organization is sending impacted individuals data breach notifications.
Oyster photocards remain valid for travel, and customers who need to renew their cards or check their journey history can still do so by contacting TfL's Customer Services.
These notifications, with one shared on Reddit, state that the following customer data may have been exposed:
- Full names
- Phone numbers
- Email addresses
- Home addresses
- Dates of birth
- Security questions and answers
TfL's current assessment is that passwords, bank and payment card details, journey information, and the names and dates of birth of children with Zip Oyster cards were not compromised.

articles.title: Nigeria’s Payaza secures Central Bank of Kenya licence - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
Nigerian payments infrastructure company Payaza has been authorised by the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) to provide payment gateway services, just weeks after getting regulatory approval in Zambia.
Payaza offers payment collection, payout and merchant tools to businesses in Africa and international markets. It handles card, mobile money and bank payments in more than 40 currencies and operates in more than 27 countries.
The CBK approval allows Payaza to operate as a licensed payment service provider in Kenya. It can now serve local merchants directly with online checkout and payment acceptance. The licence does not cover deposit-taking or customer wallets.
It comes after the Bank of Zambia gave Payaza a Certificate of Designation of a Payment System. The company has also recently picked up payment licensing milestones in China, Pakistan and Bangladesh.
“Kenya is the heartbeat of East Africa’s digital economy, and we are entering it the right way: fully licensed,” said Seyi Ebenezer, Payaza’s group CEO. “Coming so soon after our Bank of Zambia approval, this licence from the Central Bank of Kenya connects East, West and Southern Africa on one regulated platform.”
Payaza says it will now speed up merchant onboarding, build closer ties with banks and mobile money operators, and seek more licences across Africa, especially in East Africa. Nigeria makes up about 35 per cent of its revenue.

PHP on Thursday rolled out a fresh set of security patches as part of its four-week update schedule, including fixes for seven critical-severity remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities.
First in line is CVE-2026-115560, which was publicly disclosed last month, two days after PHP2Shell patches landed. Residing in the session upload progress feature, it could be triggered to write attacker data using one session serialization format and then read it using another.
“A mismatched decoder can interpret part of a session key as serialized object data. An application with a suitable object gadget chain can then execute code with the privileges of the PHP worker,” PHP’s advisory reads.
Next in line is CVE-2026-129481, described as a use-after-free that occurs after a session shutdown has been interrupted, and which PHP describes as an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-109619, one of the two PHP2Shell flaws fixed in October and now widely exploited.
“An attacker who can cause an application’s session cleanup to fail in this way may corrupt memory or crash a reused PHP worker. The use-after-free could potentially lead to remote code execution, but code execution through this specific field has not been demonstrated,” PHP notes, adding that PHP 8.2 is not affected.
Another use-after-free, CVE-2026-129182, covers additional exploitation scenarios for CVE-2026-109619, an RCE via stale global state. According to PHP, however, RCE via these scenarios has not been demonstrated.

articles.title: Beyond Pass/Fail: Characterizing Silicon Margin With PVTW
articles.summary:
Determining not only whether a device meets specification, but how far it is from the boundary, helps inform product robustness and future design decisions.
Production test is necessarily built around decisions. PASS. FAIL. Bin 1. Bin 2. Ship. Do not ship. Characterization has a different objective. It asks not only whether the device meets specification, but how far it is from the boundary.
That distinction becomes increasingly important as processors integrate compute, memory, high speed interfaces, multiple power domains and advanced packaging into increasingly complex systems.
Suppose five devices all pass the product specification, but under the same controlled workload their minimum stable operating voltages are:
0.70 V | 0.71 V | 0.73 V | 0.76 V | 0.79 V
Production test sees five passing devices. Characterization sees five different levels of margin. That changes the engineering question from “Why did this device fail?” to something potentially much more useful:
What is consuming product margin?
PVTW (process, voltage, temperature, workload) gives us a framework for exploring that question.
Take the same device and establish its voltage and frequency boundary using conventional ATE content. Then establish another boundary while running a deterministic compute workload. Repeat with SRAM, memory, PCIe and combined workloads. We may discover that the boundaries are different.

articles.title: The bottleneck just moved: why African startups should care about MCP - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
Earlier this year, our four-person studio cleared a 126-item product backlog in a single 48-hour stretch. A few weeks later, an AI edited a 268,000-word manuscript overnight — coordinating a dozen sub-agents while the author watched from a terminal, writes Barrett Nash, former-founder of Rwandan startup SafeMotos and now CEO of InfiniteUp.
Neither happened because AI suddenly got smarter. Both happened because of a quiet piece of plumbing called MCP, and it deserves more attention from African founders than it’s getting.
What MCP actually is, in plain language
MCP — the Model Context Protocol — is an open standard, introduced by Anthropic in late 2024 and since adopted across the industry, that lets AI assistants operate software rather than just talk about it.
Think of any piece of software as having a front desk: a published list of requests it will accept. MCP lets an AI walk up to those front desks itself. Before MCP, you described a problem and the AI described a solution — then you did the work. With MCP, it does the work. Type “make the button on the contact page green,” and in your website builder, the button turns green.
That’s the entire idea. Everything interesting is downstream of it.
Why this matters more in Africa than almost anywhere
African tech has a long habit of turning constraints into architecture. M-Pesa didn’t wait for branch banking; it leapfrogged it. The constraint MCP erases is headcount.

Developing software with agents is significantly harder than writing code manually, Tornhill argued. But with agentic AI, they can complete tasks two to three times faster, he added. It also helps them unblock themselves and reduces coordination needs.
Tornhill mentioned a study done on 1000+ open-source projects which showed that with AI, velocity went up during the first few weeks, but after two months the velocity gains were fully canceled out due to a massive increase in code complexity:
AI operates in a self-harm mode, often writing code it cannot reliably maintain later.
Code health measures how easy code is to understand, change, and maintain. articles.title: DDR6 memory modules could be 44% shorter than DDR5 while delivering over 50% more bandwidth
articles.summary:
Forward-looking: JEDEC is looking forward to a point when buying DRAM doesn't require selling a kidney and DDR6 is available. In an early preview of the next-gen memory standard, the organization noted that not only would it bring several upgrades, but the proposed modules would also be around 44% shorter than DDR5 versions.
As VideoCardz notes, a full-size DDR5 stick measures just over 133 mm from end to end. The design JEDEC has in mind for DDR6 measures 74 mm, putting it within a few millimeters of those little SO-DIMMs found in laptops. Unfortunately, you can probably guess who stands to benefit most from being able to squeeze more memory into the same amount of motherboard space.
Sure enough, JEDEC singles out AI inference and agentic AI as two workloads that could use more memory close to the CPU. The speed figures it gives are for registered DIMMs, the kind typically found in servers. DDR6 RDIMMs are expected to start at 12,800 MT/s, up from the 9,200 MT/s ceiling for DDR5 RDIMMs, with 14,400 MT/s and higher speeds to follow.
That works out to a roughly 39% increase in the transfer rate right from the start. There's also the data bus, which goes from 64 bits wide to 96 bits, allowing the module to move more data with each transfer. JEDEC expects those two changes to deliver more than 50% additional bandwidth at launch. It's also developing low-power modes specifically for use in data centers.

On the API side, developers can now use C# 15 union types in JSON request and response bodies across Minimal APIs and MVC. The release notes limit the feature to JSON bodies, so route, query, header, and form values cannot bind to a union.
Minimal API validation also runs asynchronous validators, which keeps threads free while a rule waits on a database lookup or a remote call. The framework can now localize validation messages and display names itself, and endpoints can skip the remaining middleware pipeline through a new [ShortCircuit] attribute.
Developers who generate OpenAPI documents now get version 3.2 unless they select an earlier one for tooling that has not caught up. As described in the release notes, the framework depends on Microsoft.OpenApi 3.3.1 for this, and the notes label that update a breaking change.
With 3.2, endpoints that stream server-sent events are documented with a schema for each event's payload, and the generator emits an anyOf schema for unions. It has none of the 3D or ray-tracing hardware you'd find on a regular graphics card; instead, the chip – now sold as the GPU D270 – spends that space on AI and scientific work. Until this week, though, Intel hadn't really shown how fast it is. That changed at the SC26 supercomputing show in Chicago.
In a post, Intel put the D270 up against Nvidia's RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell Server Edition. Instead of games or AI models, Intel went with something a little more niche. It picked four workloads that banks rely on to put a price on financial contracts.
Across those four, the D270 delivered between 1.92 and 5.9 times the performance of Nvidia's card. Its biggest win showed up in a European Monte Carlo simulation. Intel's card also did all of this at just 350W, compared to the 600W that Nvidia's card is rated for.
All four tests rely on double-precision, or FP64, calculations. Intel's Xe3P architecture handles those calculations at full speed, so the D270 barely slows down when a task needs that extra accuracy. That full-speed FP64 support is where most of the D270's lead over Nvidia's card comes from.
The RTX Pro 6000, on the other hand, uses the same chip as the GeForce RTX 5090. That silicon only handles FP64 at a tiny fraction of its usual speed, so by sticking to FP64-heavy workloads, Intel chose the kind of tests where Nvidia's card was likely to fall behind.

Agent security is product security, and your marketing site counts
A marketing site used to have two kinds of visitors: people and search crawlers. Now an agent can build a page, a second agent can scrape it, a third can summarize it for a potential customer, and a fourth can optimize it overnight after studying yesterday’s traffic.
“The ones that you do not control make the marketing site a product with agent users, and products need product security.”
You control some of these agents but not all the data they ingest and train on. The ones that you do not control make the marketing site a product with agent users, and products need product security. A marketing site is usually public with no login required to view or break. Adversaries go after whether the site still says what you wrote, serves what you built, and reports what real visitors did. This article calls those content integrity, delivery integrity, and signal integrity, and looks at where each kind of agent touches them.
Five agents, three kinds of integrity

- build,
- read or scrape,
- analyze its visitor data,
- optimize the site from that data,
- adversarial agents that attack
Each role touches at least one of three things worth protecting the integrity of:

articles.title: Scientific simulation meets AI sovereignty and the CLOUD Act - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Enterprises fear AI success more than failure, because success means lock-in they can’t escape
The supercomputing world built its reputation on scientific simulation, but the artificial intelligence infrastructure now filling the same data centers raises a harder question. When models turn data into revenue, control over that data and the intelligence it produces becomes a board-level concern few companies discuss publicly.

The baseline for that fact-finding, as anyone tasked with investigating these incidents will tell you, is that the vast majority of these digital breakdowns are not the result of malicious intent but rather casualties of IT admins’ constant war to keep computer systems from collapsing under the weight of their own complexity.
“I’ve just seen enough times where we thought maybe it’s a cyberattack and it turns out it’s not. Sometimes it will be, but typically not,” says Matthew Prince, CEO of the Internet infrastructure company Cloudflare. “Right now, most of what we’re seeing is the standard background noise. Stuff breaks, and that’s just the nature of complex systems.”

Dass die Betreiber überhaupt haftbar gemacht werden sollten, begründet Simon damit, dass die Modellbetreiber selbst die Voraussetzungen für die sogenannten Ausbrüche von KI-Systemen aus ihren Sandboxes geschaffen haben.
Die Diskussionen um die Entschleunigung bei der KI-Entwicklung, die zuletzt auch Anthropic-Chef Amodei forderte, scheinen Simon zufolge schon wieder vorbei zu sein. Eine persönliche, körperliche Haftung könne eher dafür sorgen, dass „Sorgfalt in diese Systeme Einzug hält und diese Beschleunigung vielleicht gebremst wird“.

articles.title: Where should AI workloads run? Probably next to the data.
articles.summary:
Where should AI workloads run? Probably next to the data.
AWS raised prices on EC2 Capacity Blocks, its reserved GPU capacity, by about 15% in January and about 20% in July. Picture a platform team watching a training job’s bill climb after copying a few hundred terabytes of sensor data across regions just to reach the GPUs, then realizing the data never had to move.
For AI workloads, the real question is whether the workload goes to the data or the data goes to the workload. Data gravity usually answers it.
Data gravity hits AI workloads harder than it ever hit analytics
Data gravity is the tendency of compute, applications, and services to be pulled toward large concentrations of data, because moving the data costs more than moving the logic that processes it. The larger a dataset grows, the more expensive every copy becomes, and the more everything that needs that data ends up living next to it.
Scheduled BI often tolerates periodic queries against sampled or aggregated data. Large training runs can require repeated reads of a much larger dataset, while agents retrieve fresh context throughout a workflow. When those reads cross regions or environments, transfer costs and latency add up. Each agent output also becomes new data that feeds the next round of retrieval, which compounds the pull over time.

Meet Google's latest quality criteria, which will essentially force developers to better support foldables even if they did not plan to.
Google recently published the new "adaptive quality standards" Android developers will be required to adopt over the next few months. The change will affect apps published on the Google Play Store, with a specific focus on improving support for the latest foldable devices coming to Android.
Google said that customers are paying a premium for their cracking new foldable devices, and are consequently going to expect a similarly premium app experience. Developers will just have to adapt, or they are going to risk being demoted in Google Play's app promotion programs.
The main requirement is that apps will need to meet the "Tier 3" baseline in Android's official adaptive quality guidelines. Tier 3 apps are "adaptive ready" experiences, which means they will have to completely fill a foldable's display area without letterboxing effects or compatibility modes. Furthermore, Tier 3 apps will have to preserve text or playback state during rotation or folding, while supporting multi-window environments at the same time.

Pakistan undersea cable failure causes internet outage near Strait of Hormuz — fault detected offshore weeks after Iran threatened infrastructure in the region
Pakistan's telecommunications authority says that Transworld Associates is looking into what caused the issue and when it expects it to be fixed, but traffic has been rerouted for now.
Pakistan's telecommunications authority, the PTA, has confirmed that internet connectivity issues affecting the country's residents are related to the failure of an international submarine cable. SEA-ME-WE 5 is located almost seven miles off the coast of Pakistan, near the Gulf of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz, and connects the region with European networks via the Middle East. The TWA says that the outage may have caused intermittent connectivity issues and a decline in service quality, with Transworld Associates (TWA) working to identify the cause of the issue. No timeframe has been provided for when a fix will be available yet, but for now, internet traffic has been rerouted to minimize the impact of the outage.
The outage comes weeks after the Islamic Republic of Iran described several undersea fiber cables that run through the Strait of Hormuz as "legitimate new targets" in the ongoing tensions in the area. February's start of military action by the United States, Israel, and others has made the Strait of Hormuz a household name in recent months. articles.title: NASA's new Moon plans have a problem: Orion wasn't designed to fly this way
articles.summary:
NASA recently announced a significant shakeup to the Artemis program that will land humans on the Moon.
The moves were designed to give the agency’s lunar lander providers—SpaceX with its Starship vehicle, and Blue Origin with Blue Moon—more flexibility in reaching the Moon. For Starship, this means docking with Orion in Earth orbit, and then traveling to the Moon in tandem. For Blue Moon, it shifts the rendezvous with Orion all the way to low-lunar orbit.
These changes benefit the lunar landers, but in turn impose more of a burden on the Orion spacecraft, which is built for NASA by Lockheed Martin. To understand the implications for the spacecraft, Ars spoke with Kirk Shireman, Human Spaceflight Exploration and Orion program manager at Lockheed.
Starship challenges
For Starship, the evolved plan has SpaceX fueling a Starship lunar lander in low-Earth orbit before docking with Orion in high-Earth orbit. The crew will fly to the Moon on board Orion before two of the four astronauts transfer into Starship for a landing on the Moon.
Due to the docking configuration with Starship, Orion must now fly backward to the Moon, with its Service Module at the top of the stack. This is a fundamentally different flying posture than Orion was designed for, Shireman said, and creates issues for Orion’s propulsion system.

articles.title: Fuite de données chez Chargemap : des millions de conducteurs sont touchés par une cyberattaque

Chargemap prévient tous les conducteurs concernés par mail. Consulté par 01net, le courriel révèle que l’application a été « la cible d’une attaque informatique » le 8 novembre 2026. Pour ceux qui ne connaissent pas, Chargemap est une application française très utilisée par les conducteurs de véhicules électriques. Le nombre de comptes touchés n’a pas été communiqué par l’entreprise originaire de Strasbourg.

Une faille sur une ancienne interface

articles.title: Los nacidos entre 1960 y 1970 pueden cobrar el 100% de la pensión, pero necesitan haber cotizado estos años
articles.summary:
Quienes han nacido entre 1960 y 1970 ya no tienen tan lejos la jubilación, y por eso es un buen momento para repasar cuánto aspiran a cobrar y los años cotizados que necesitan para llegar al 100% de la pensión. El número de años cotizados es uno de los factores que más pesan, porque marca tanto la edad a la que puedes retirarte como el porcentaje de la base reguladora que te corresponde.
Si vemos los datos de la edad de jubilación, durante 2026 hacen falta 36 años y seis meses de cotización para cobrar ese 100%, y a partir de 2027 el listón sube a 37 años. Pero cobrar la pensión máxima también depende de las bases por las que hayas cotizado a lo largo de tu vida laboral.
Cuántos años hacen falta para el 100% y para jubilarse a los 65
La pensión se calcula combinando los años cotizados con la base reguladora, que a su vez se obtiene a partir de las bases de cotización del trabajador durante un periodo concreto. Según las tablas de la Ley General de la Seguridad Social, los primeros 15 años cotizados dan derecho al 50% de la base reguladora, y a partir de ahí cada mes adicional va sumando un pequeño porcentaje hasta completar el 100%.
Otra cosa que cuenta es la edad ordinaria de jubilación, que el calendario de la reforma de las pensiones va subiendo poco a poco hasta llegar a los 67 años en 2027 para quienes no acrediten suficiente cotización. articles.title: Son pedigree est déjà bien chargé : c’est quoi ARTEX, l’outil de piratage chinois utilisé contre la Commission européenne ?
articles.summary:
Le voici sur le devant de la scène médiatique… européenne.
Le 19 novembre 2026, Politico a révélé que le service de cybersécurité des institutions européennes avait détecté l’utilisation d’ARTEX dans une campagne de cyberattaques visant la Commission européenne.
Depuis plus de dix jours, cette attaque perturbe plusieurs services internes de la Commission, de la plateforme RH aux services de traduction en passant par l’outil de remboursement des frais médicaux.
L’outil n’a pourtant rien d’un inconnu dans l’écosystème cyber. Le CERT-EU lui avait consacré une note technique dès le 5 novembre, le FBI a publié une alerte le 13, et les grands éditeurs de cybersécurité suivent sa diffusion depuis la fin de l’été.
Qu’est-ce qu’ARTEX ?
Sur le papier, l’intention était bonne. ARTEX a en effet été conçu comme un outil de test d’intrusion (pentest), qui simule des attaques pour qu’une organisation découvre ses failles avant les pirates. S’il est présenté comme un outil d’IA, ARTEX n’est pas un modèle en lui-même. C’est une surcouche qui se branche sur des modèles existants, de Claude à DeepSeek, ou sur n’importe quel service compatible avec l’interface d’OpenAI.
Il fait travailler ensemble plusieurs agents, entre lesquels un module de planification répartit les tâches de l’intrusion, et chacun consigne ses découvertes dans un journal commun. Un opérateur humain les dirige et reprend la main aux moments décisifs. Ces agents scannent le réseau visé, exploitent les failles trouvées, install…

articles.title: Keep inference running through regional capacity shortfalls with cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Keep inference running through regional capacity shortfalls with cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI
Serving a model from more than one AWS Region is a well-established pattern for highly available inference: when one Region runs short of GPU capacity, requests move to another. The pattern is simple to describe and hard to operate. Until now, if you served models on Amazon SageMaker AI managed endpoints, cross-Region routing was a piece you still had to build yourself.
Today, we’re introducing cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI. It uses a new resource, the inference router, that gives your application one invocation path across the endpoints and inference components you already run, in one or more AWS Regions and AWS accounts. You register the destinations that serve a model, and your application invokes the router instead of a specific endpoint. The router keeps requests in its own Region while the local destination is healthy, shifts new requests to another registered destination when it isn’t, and returns traffic gradually after recovery.
In this post, we explain how cross-Region inference routing decides where each request runs, walk through an example with one model in two Regions, and cover monitoring, limits, and what you pay. For a cross-account deployment that serves several models, see How Salesforce is advancing global-scale model serving with cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI.

articles.title: Meta’s AI agent Muse is mixing up conversations and could be exposing private data, report says | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Meta employees have raised concerns that the company’s AI agent Muse has been mixing up conversations across different accounts and exposing private user data, according to a new Reuters report that looked at internal company posts.
In some of these instances, employees said Muse surfaced messages about childcare requests they never made, career advice they never asked for, product orders they never placed, and bank account balances that didn’t belong to them.
One employee told colleagues that Muse had randomly sent an extra message in a chat about weather and tide information, saying: “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”
In another example, an employee using the AI agent on her personal phone received a reminder from Muse to respond to a message from her sister on Signal, the popular end-to-end encrypted messaging app.
“This seems like an extreme privacy violation. I definitely did not grant it access to other apps, or recall being asked about this,” the employee said in her post, according to the report.
“Employee testing is core to the product development process and the entire point is to get feedback, so we can implement safety and privacy protections and improve products,” a Meta spokesperson said in an email to TechCrunch. “Importantly, employees have access to different versions of Muse than the public, so they’re often reviewing features, functionality, and behavior not available elsewhere.”

articles.title: Desativou o histórico do Gemini? O Google salva mesmo assim • Tecnoblog
articles.summary:
Desativou o histórico do Gemini? O Google salva mesmo assim
Empresa atualizou tempo que suas conversas na IA ficam registradas de três dias para dois meses, independente da configuração de histórico.
O Gemini agora “lembra” seus últimos dois meses de consultas na plataforma, mesmo que você tenha desativado completamente seu histórico. O Google atualizou suas políticas de privacidade para a inteligência artificial na terça-feira (17/11) e aumentou o tempo que suas interações ficam salvas: de 72 horas para dois meses.
Você ainda pode ajustar por quanto tempo deseja reter as trocas. A configuração dá a opção padrão de 18 meses, além de opções de três ou 36 meses, além de deixar esse limite indefinido ou totalmente zerado (mas nem tanto). Independente da sua escolha, a nova política garante pelo menos dois meses de mensagens salvas.
Segundo o Google, a mudança tem como objetivo usar as interações para “proteger o Google, seus usuários e o público”. Ao avisar sobre a novidade, a empresa fala ainda em “ajuda de revisores humanos”, dando a entender que pessoas reais teriam acesso ao que você pergunta ao Gemini.
O acesso às informações trocadas com a IA não é uma novidade. Uma recomendação comumente dada por especialistas na área, inclusive, é não fornecer dados sensíveis nessas consultas à IA, como números de cartão de crédito, documentos, entre outros exemplos.
A revisão dessas mensagens por humanos também é algo padrão das IAs, e está previsto na política de privacidade do Google.…

From learning to leaderboard: How Cisco upskilled 1,200 engineers in agentic AI with AWS AI League

Engineers learn fastest when they build something real, see it fail, fix it, and try again.

Exclusive: Fig Security partners with Elastic to show how data changes affect detection coverage
Security operations startup Fig Security Inc. today announced an integration partnership with Elastic N.V. that it says gives security teams visibility into how data changes affect their detection coverage.
The partnership sees Fig’s capabilities for mapping detection dependencies now integrating with Elastic Security, the open security operations platform from Elastic. The platform offers prebuilt integrations and detection rules to establish coverage from day one, with Fig claimed to help security operations engineers safeguard that coverage as their environments evolve.
Detection rules are dependent on data arriving in the structure they expect, including the fields and values needed to identify suspicious activity. According to Fig, those dependencies can break when changes are made in tools that the security team does not own. The resulting problem, which Fig calls drift, leaves rules active while the data feeding them is missing the information needed to catch an attack.
Once connected through a read-only application programming interface key, Fig’s Security Data Lineage feature maps an Elastic environment’s sources through pipelines, mappings and fields to the detection rules that use them. Any change to a source, pipeline or mapping is said to have Fig identify the affected detections, along with a suggested repair.

articles.title: Una herramienta de Microsoft escondía malware capaz de robar claves de GitHub y Azure
articles.summary:
Una herramienta oficial de Microsoft para Python fue modificada para robar datos de las personas que la instalaran. El problema afectó a las versiones 1.26.1 y 1.26.2 de agent-framework, un programa que ayuda a crear asistentes de inteligencia artificial. Ambas versiones se publicaron en PyPI, un sitio donde los programadores descargan herramientas para sus proyectos.
El malware podía buscar contraseñas, archivos de acceso y otros datos guardados en la computadora. También apuntaba a cuentas y servicios usados por desarrolladores, como GitHub y Azure. GitHub permite guardar y compartir código; Azure es una plataforma de Microsoft para alojar programas y manejar servicios en internet. The Register informó que investigadores de seguridad descubrieron el problema y que Microsoft puso algunos repositorios en privado mientras investigaba.
No hacía falta abrir la herramienta para que actuara
Según los investigadores citados por The Register, el malware podía empezar a funcionar cuando se iniciaba Python en una computadora que tuviera instalada una de las versiones afectadas. Python es el lenguaje con el que se escriben ciertos programas. articles.title: IDrive wants to back up your coding agents, too
articles.summary:
IDrive wants to back up your coding agents, too
Coding agents need backups, too, or at least that’s what IDrive is arguing.
Backup and storage service IDrive on Thursday announced AI Agents Backup, a feature in its desktop app that finds the data these agents store locally for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Cline and copies it to the user’s IDrive account.
By default, agents tend to keep a lot of their state on a developer’s machine, including session transcripts, instruction files, and MCP server configurations. The problem is that most of this sits in hidden folders that developers rarely look at.
Thing is, some of this data is actually valuable.
